title: Diagonal pair associated to proper flat duality over a qcqs base
statement: Let $S$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme and $f:X\to S$ proper, flat and of finite presentation [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $a$ be a right adjoint to $Rf_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(X)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(S)$ [def-pc-derived-category], [def-pc-derived-direct-image]. Set $K=a(\mathcal O_S)$. Then $K$ is pseudo-coherent and locally has finite Tor amplitude over $S$, and there is a canonical diagonal class $\xi_a$ for which $(K,\xi_a)$ is a coherent relative dualizing pair [def-trf-coherent-relative-dualizing-pair]. More precisely, if $p_1,p_2:X\times_SX\to X$, $b$ is right adjoint to $Rp_{2,*}$ and $c$ is right adjoint to $R\Delta_*$, then $b(\mathcal O_X)\simeq Lp_1^*K$ by proper flat base change, $cb\simeq\mathrm{id}$ by adjunction composition, and $\xi_a$ is the diagonal-coinduction adjunct of $\mathcal O_X\simeq c(Lp_1^*K)$. Under the canonical proper-flat right-adjoint base-change isomorphisms for maps $S'\to S$ of qcqs schemes, the induced pair is identified with the derived pullback pair. In particular these classes agree on base-open overlaps and are preserved by trace-preserving identifications of right-adjoint images. No Noetherian or smoothness assumption is made.

source.place: Tags 0E4L (lemma-properties-relative-dualizing), 0E2P (lemma-van-den-bergh, equation-pre-rigid), 0E2Z (lemma-flat-proper-relative-dualizing), and 0E4P (remark-relative-dualizing-complex-bis); canonical class compatibility by the adjunction mates in those constructions.

proof.text: Work with structure-module complexes, not constant torsion coefficients. Properness makes the diagonal closed. The projections of $P=X\times_SX$ and the pullbacks of $f$ to affine opens of $S$ are proper and flat, by proper base change and pointwise flatness under base change. They remain locally finitely presented: on an affine chart, base change carries a presentation $R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(r_1,\ldots,r_m)$ to the same finite presentation over the new ring. The finite-presentation convention includes quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. Thus $X,P$ and all these proper pullbacks over qcqs bases are qcqs: finite affine covers of the base have quasi-compact inverse images, and quasi-separatedness is checked by the closed relative diagonal and the quasi-compact diagonal of the base. We can therefore choose the projection and diagonal right adjoints on $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}$.

source.place: Tags 0AAB (lemma-proper-flat-base-change), 0E2P (lemma-van-den-bergh), setup; qcqs right adjoints are Tag 0A9E (lemma-twisted-inverse-image).

proof.text: For every affine open $V\subset S$, proper-flat right-adjoint base change identifies $K|_{X_V}$ with $a_V(\mathcal O_V)$. The exact Zariski--etale equivalence intertwines direct images and sends structure modules to structure modules, so transporting its adjunction Hom bijection identifies $\epsilon_{X_V}^*a_V(\mathcal O_V)$ with the etale right-adjoint unit image. Apply the affine adjoint-unit theorem to obtain its pseudo-coherence and local finite relative Tor amplitude. Etale pseudo-coherence descent gives pseudo-coherence of $K|_{X_V}$; the relative Tor comparison gives local finite Tor dimension over $V$ on the Zariski site. These statements are local on $X$, so the inverse images of the affine opens prove both claims for $K$ over $S$. Testing each local relative Tor interval against the inverse-image ring itself bounds the cohomology of $K$ on that open. A finite subcover of the qcqs scheme $X$ gives a global lower bound. The flat projection $p_1$ preserves it: at each stalk its tensor pullback is tensor with a flat local ring, which preserves the kernel/image sequences defining cohomology. Thus its termwise pullback preserves quasi-isomorphisms and computes derived pullback, and $H^i(Lp_1^*K)=p_1^*H^i(K)$. Consequently $M=Lp_1^*K$ is bounded below. No Noetherian affine charts are used.

source.place: Tag 0E4L (lemma-properties-relative-dualizing), clause (1); spaces-perfect.tex Tags 08HE and 0DK7 for the site comparison.

proof.text: Take $b$ right adjoint to $Rp_{2,*}$ and $c$ right adjoint to $R\Delta_*$. Proper-flat right-adjoint base change for the square with both bottom and right maps equal to $f$ gives $b(\mathcal O_X)\simeq Lp_1^*a(\mathcal O_S)=M$. Derived direct-image composition identifies $Rp_{2,*}R\Delta_*$ with the identity because $p_2\Delta=\mathrm{id}_X$. The right-adjoint composition theorem, including its unit and counit normalization, identifies $cb$ with the identity. Evaluate its inverse at $\mathcal O_X$ and then use $b(\mathcal O_X)\simeq M$ to obtain an isomorphism $h:\mathcal O_X\xrightarrow{\sim}c(M)$. Define $\xi_a=\varepsilon^\Delta_M\circ R\Delta_*h$. This is the specified diagonal-coinduction adjunct, with no choice of an additional scalar.

source.place: Tag 0E2P (lemma-van-den-bergh), equation-pre-rigid, with the unit object rather than the tensor-square equation.

proof.text: Apply closed-section coinduction to $p=p_2$, $i=\Delta$, and the bounded-below object $M$ from step 2. Its normalized isomorphism identifies $R\Delta_*h$ with multiplication by $\xi_a$ as a map $\Delta_*\mathcal O_X\to R\mathcal Hom_P(\Delta_*\mathcal O_X,M)$. Since $h$ is an isomorphism, so are its image and this multiplication map. Together with step 2, these are exactly the three requirements in the supplied coherent relative dualizing-pair definition. In particular this checks the actual multiplication class, rather than merely an unspecified isomorphism of the two objects.

Write $\beta:b(\mathcal O_X)\xrightarrow{\sim}M$ for the comparison in step 3. Under $R\Delta_*\dashv c$ and then $Rp_{2,*}\dashv b$, the composite-adjunction normalization says precisely that $j=\beta^{-1}\xi_a:\Delta_*\mathcal O_X\to b(\mathcal O_X)$ corresponds to $\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal O_X}$. Equivalently,
$$\varepsilon^b_{\mathcal O_X}\circ Rp_{2,*}(j)=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal O_X},$$
using $Rp_{2,*}\Delta_*\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_X$. The adjunction is a bijection on Hom sets, so this equation determines $j$ uniquely. This furnishes a second characterization of the class without any assertion about uniqueness of arbitrary dualizing pairs.

source.place: Tag 0E2P, equation-pre-rigid: composite adjunction evaluated at the identity.

proof.text:
Let $g:S'\to S$ have qcqs source, put $h=g_X:X'\to X$, and $t:P'=X'\times_{S'}X'\to P$. The pullback-pair theorem supplies $d:Lt^*\Delta_*\mathcal O_X\simeq\Delta'_*\mathcal O_{X'}$ and the pulled class. The square $(p_2,h)$ is cartesian: $P'\simeq P\times_X X'$. Write $B:Lt^*b(\mathcal O_X)\simeq b'(\mathcal O_{X'})$ for proper-flat right-adjoint base change and set $j_g=B\circ Lt^*j\circ d^{-1}$. By its definition [def-sc-duality-equation-base-change-map], $B$ is the composite of $Lt^*b$ of the unit of $Lh^*\dashv Rh_*$, the inverse of the conjugate $\theta$ of the ordinary base-change map $\beta_{p_2}:Lh^*Rp_{2,*}\to Rp'_{2,*}Lt^*$ (invertible by [lem-sc-proper-flat-right-adjoint-basechange-hbeta] for the proper flat finitely presented $p_2$ over the qcqs $X$), and the counit of $Lt^*\dashv Rt_*$; unwinding the conjugate gives $\varepsilon^{b'}\circ Rp'_{2,*}(B)=Lh^*(\varepsilon^b)\circ\beta_{p_2}^{-1}$. This counit formula, with the pasted-square law, gives
$$\varepsilon^{b'}\circ Rp'_{2,*}(j_g)=Lh^*(\varepsilon^b\circ Rp_{2,*}j)=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal O_{X'}}.$$
Here the ordinary direct-image base-change arrows and the composite $p_2\Delta=\mathrm{id}$ cancel by mate pasting and its identity clause; no invertibility of a diagonal exceptional base-change map is required. Step 5 over $S'$ now gives $j_g=j'$. Finally paste the self-product base-change square $(f,f)$ with $g$ in the two orders. The same mate-pasting law identifies $Lp_1'^*(Lh^*K\simeq a'(\mathcal O_{S'}))\circ Lt^*\beta$ with $\beta'\circ B$, after pullback associators. Multiplying $j_g=j'$ by these comparisons proves that the proper-flat right-adjoint base-change isomorphism carries the pulled $\xi_a$ to $\xi_{a'}$.

proof.text: For base-open overlaps use step 6 with the overlap mapping to $S$ (or an affine open cover of the overlap). Its class is the pullback of the same global class. The identity and iterated-pullback clauses of the pair base-change theorem identify the two successive restrictions, so they agree. For another adjunction choice, the canonical comparison between right adjoints has the pasted counit normalization of the right-adjoint composition theorem; applying it to the identity in step 5 preserves $j$ and hence $\xi_a$. More generally a trace-preserving isomorphism $\alpha:a(\mathcal O_S)\to\widetilde a(\mathcal O_S)$ satisfies $\widetilde\varepsilon\,Rf_*\alpha=\varepsilon$. Under $Rf_*\dashv\widetilde a$ this equality says that $\alpha$ is the unique adjunct of $\varepsilon$, hence is the component of that canonical adjoint comparison. It therefore preserves the diagonal class too.
